svg.title: sky jobs launch (6 nodes): ej-prj-i2-3 sequence diagram
svg.text: the 4 new commits, then what is left
An empty result means "not checked", so each jobs.launch re-runs the
check. The phase numbers here date from when it took ≈4.7 s. A later
profile found 1.1 s and phase A at 3.5 s, nearly all GCP with expired
credentials. Why it changed is not confirmed.
no change aimed at this step
It fell 1.2 s anyway. This run does not show why.
time.sleep(1) between polls: about 0.5 s lost on average after
A Kubernetes watch ends the wait once every waiting pod runs
or one is going away. The poll still decides; a watch failure
serial pull checks with imagePullPolicy: Always
On one kind node, the kubelet ran 6 pull checks in turn: 3.41 s in an
earlier trace. Not in this run, since both arms used IfNotPresent.
ray stop only if Ray runs
ray stop only if Ray runs
uv skips bytecode by default, so every pod compiled Ray on
.pyc files in the image, compiled at build time.
Cost: 160 MB larger on disk, 34 MB larger compressed. Applies once a
do not import Ray Serve in ray start
ray start imported ray.serve.scripts just to register a
command, pulling in pandas and FastAPI on every pod.
A Ray patch registers `ray serve` lazily. apply_patches.py
finds files with find_spec, so it does not import Serve
With the watch: GCS first log 5.82 → 3.37 s, last raylet 14.22
Ray starts before SkyPilot is prepared; pins pre-installed in the
image; ray stop runs only if Ray is running.
Setup 3.60 (1.6–17.5) → 1.82 (1.4–2.3) s. uv --dry-run holds the venv
lock while it waits on PyPI, and the install queues behind it. Not
fixed: the calmer range may be PyPI that night.
One blocking Ray wait, with skylet started alongside it.
where the big drop shows up
Ray wait + skylet 16.28 → 4.33 s, the largest stage gain.
Skylet alone went 1.60 → 2.46 s. Fork commit b7eff791e targets it, and
each head call is a new exec + Python
Launched → submitted 3.85 → 3.34 s. An earlier trace: set_autostop
bytecode also helps the job itself
Published image trace, first job: 8.32 s, of which the slowest
node loading the task function took 3.63 s.
E fell 2.2 s with gRPC off. This run does not split it by
commit, so bytecode is the likely cause, not a proven one.
the queue call and worker imports
Queue → driver took 1.82 s in that trace, nearly all of it the kubectl
exec. Workers also import sky modules for the task.
gRPC: queue 1.71 → 0.04 s. Drop sky imports on workers.
keep job timestamps exact over gRPC
A protobuf float holds a current Unix time only to the nearest
128 s. With gRPC on, a short job's duration was 0 s.
New optional double field; a skylet without it falls back to
None here, since gRPC is off. A correctness fix: durations
0.00 → 6.32–6.82 s with gRPC on, which removes a blocker to
enabling it. gRPC wall time 48.8 → 45.6 s (p = 0.052).
Status and submitted-at come from one head command.
Skip the uniform(0, 15) s sleep for a job already seen finished. Base
3.7–16.1 s; i2-3 is 3.2–3.3 s in 7 of 8 runs, and candidate_b2_1 took
Reuse the terminal status seen at launch and fetch the end
The follower re-checks status when the controller logs, rather than
Client total (sky jobs launch, 6 nodes, 8 interleaved runs per arm)
Remaining: submit 7.2 s · hand-off 5.2 s · provision 14.6 s · job 6.6 s · checks 2.4 + 3.3 s
Medians do not add up across phases. kind on one machine; no cold-node image pull.
sky jobs launch on Kubernetes (6 nodes): where the new optimizations apply
UML sequence (consolidation mode, kind, 6 nodes) · medians of 8 interleaved runs per arm · 5ef55efa4 + published image → ej-prj-i2-3 16738238e + bytecode image · both IfNotPresent, gRPC off
Phase numbers compare the base with all changes, including earlier branches. Most "Gain" lines come from a commit's own A/B. Green phase = p < 0.05; grey = not significant.
Solid arrow = call · dashed arrow = return/read · grey bars = activation · par/alt/loop = UML combined fragments
